Subject ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE.

Made by D.S.I. MAKLAWSKY Forwarded by D.I. GLOVER.

Sir,

At 10 p.m. July 25th. 1938, D.S.I. Umemoto of the
S.P.Office informed the undersigned of the request of
Sergeant-Major Katoda of the Japanese Gendarmerie to
render assistance in effecting the arrest of one Zung
Hsi Tsung (陈希曾) formerly Chief of S.C.G.Police Bureau,
Nantso, who, it was believed, was going to leave Shanghai
for Hongkong at 11 p.m. from the Customs Jetty per tender
Scot 1, to board the S.S. "EMPRESS OF ASIA".

According to D.S.I. Umemoto, Zung Hsi Tsung is wanted
by the Japanese Gendarmerie in connection with terroristic
activities.

Assistance was rendered by D.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung
and the undersigned and careful watch was kept at the
Customs Jetty up to 11 p.m., departure of the tender
Scot 1., but Zung Hsi Tsung did not put in an appearance.

I am, Sir
Yours obediently,

〔签名：Maklawsky〕
D. S. I.

先生，

1938年7月25日晚上10时，特别警务办公室（S.P.Office）副督察梅本（Umemoto）通知卑职，日本宪兵队加藤（Katoda）军曹长请求协助逮捕前南市上海中国警察局（S.C.G.Police Bureau, Nantso）局长陈希曾（Zung Hsi Tsung），据信他将于当晚11时从海关码头乘坐“Scot 1”号小轮前往香港，转乘“亚细亚皇后”号（EMPRESS OF ASIA）轮船。

据梅本副督察称，日本宪兵队因恐怖活动嫌疑通缉陈希曾。

宋秉宗（Soong Ping Tsung）副督察和卑职提供了协助，并在海关码头严密监视直至晚上11时“Scot 1”号小轮离港，但陈希曾并未出现。

此致，
先生，

Assistance to Japanese Military Police.

At 8-30am. on 5/7/38 Mr. S. Suzuki of the
Japanese Military Police and Chinese detectives in his
employ came to this station with a male Chinese named
Wong Kyung Pau(王金宝), 21, Tungchow, residing
Tsau Ka Doo, Jessfield, who had been arrested by the
Japanese Authorities for armed robbery committed in
the Tsau Ka Doo area, O.O.L.

Assistance was requested to visit Room No. 148 of
the Tung Sang(通商) Hotel, No.42 Avenue Road to
arrest two accomplices in the armed robbery.

D.S. Smith, C.D.C. 332 and the undersigned
accompanied the party, and it was found that the
wanted men had vacated the room on 4/7/38.

No further action was taken.

June 23, 1938. Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Pao :-

CHINESE MOBILE UNITS PUSHING DRIVE TOWARDS SHANGHAI

The Chinese mobile units are again very active along the Nanking-Shanghai and Shanghai-Hangchow Railways. An extensive guerrilla warfare has been launched by the mobile units beyond Lunghwa and on the border of Kiangsu and Chekiang Provinces between Sungkiang and Feng Kyung (楓涇). Railway tracks at these places have been destroyed and as a result railway communication between Shanghai and Kashing is once more interrupted. The Japanese are experiencing much difficulty in coping with the situation.
It is said that the Chinese mobile units are pushing on their drive towards Shanghai.

Attack on Japanese Launch

At about nightfall on June 21 when the Japanese launch "Quinsan Maru," with a boat in tow, was passing by Chwang Ka Kyung (莊家) along the Soochow Creek in the western district of Shanghai, it was attacked from both sides of the creek by Chinese guerrillas, resulting in the wounding of more than 10 Japanese on board.
Following the attack, a number of Japanese soldiers were rushed to the place and a vigorous search was conducted in the villages at Kiang Kiao (江橋), Chi Wang Miao (紀王廟) and Yu Chi Tung (虞姬墩) in the vicinity of Chwang Ka Kyung. A number of houses which were suspected of being used as hiding places by the Chinese guerrillas were destroyed.

Standard :-

AN INTERRUPTED MARRIAGE FEAST

On the night of June 21 a tense melodrama was enacted between the Japanese authorities and Chinese traitors at the Dah Ka Lee Restaurant (大加利) on Peking Road.
On the evening in question a feast was being given at the restaurant to celebrate the marriage of Chang Tseng-ih (張正一), age 27, of the Bureau of Communications of the Shanghai Municipal Administration, who is the grandson of Chang Shih-chow (張雪洲), age 81, Chairman of the Chamber of Commerce at Chowpu (周浦), Pootung. The bridegroom's former wife, who did not wish to be a daughter-in-law of a traitor, had eloped with her sweetheart named Ma (馬) and joined the mobile units at Au Sha (下沙).
Acting on false information that certain members of the mobile units were giving an entertainment at the Dah Ka Lee Restaurant, the Japanese authorities at 8.20 p.m. detailed ten special service officers to the restaurant in company with Chinese and foreign detectives

1938年6月23日。晨间翻译。

《大美报》:-

中国流动部队向上海推进

中国流动部队在京沪铁路和沪杭铁路沿线再次非常活跃。流动部队在龙华以外以及江苏省和浙江省之间松江和枫泾 (Feng Kyung) 边境地区发动了大规模的游击战。这些地方的铁轨被破坏，导致上海和嘉兴之间的铁路交通再次中断。日本人应对局势困难重重。
据说中国流动部队正向上海推进。

袭击日本汽艇

6月21日黄昏时分，当日本汽艇“昆山丸”号 (Quinsan Maru) 拖着一艘小船经过上海西区苏州河沿岸的莊家 (Chwang Ka Kyung) 时，遭到河岸两侧中国游击队的袭击，导致船上10多名日本人受伤。
袭击发生后，多名日本士兵迅速赶往事发地，并在莊家附近的江橋 (Kiang Kiao)、紀王廟 (Chi Wang Miao) 和虞姬墩 (Yu Chi Tung) 等村庄进行了 vigorous 搜索。一些被怀疑为中国游击队藏身处的房屋被摧毁。

《标准晚报》:-

被打断的婚宴

6月21日晚，日本当局与中国汉奸在北京路的大加利餐厅 (Dah Ka Lee Restaurant) 上演了一出紧张的闹剧。
当晚，该餐厅正在举办宴会，庆祝上海市政府交通局27岁的张正一 (Chang Tseng-ih) 的婚礼，他是浦东周浦 (Chowpu) 81岁商会主席张雪洲 (Chang Shih-chow) 的孙子。新郎的前妻不愿做汉奸的儿媳，已与名为马 (Ma) 的情人私奔，并加入了下沙 (Au Sha) 的流动部队。
日本当局根据错误情报，称某些流动部队成员正在大加利餐厅举行娱乐活动，于晚上8时20分派遣十名特务人员，会同中外侦探前往该餐厅

from Central Police Station. The raiding party went
upstairs. The Japanese officers produced pistols and
ordered all the persons in the room not to move. The
guests were greatly alarmed because some of them had
been discussing the murder at the Tung Shing Lou
Restaurant (同兴酒楼) on Foochow Road. The Police
officers courteously requested all the lady guests to
gather in one room to await examination. All the men
were then searched three times but nothing of an
incriminating nature was found.
The Japanese officers were mystified.
After some questioning, they learned that the host was
a peace-abiding and pro-Japanese citizen. Still they
were not convinced and took the host, the bridegroom
and the guests to the Central Police Station for
interrogation. As Chang Shih-chow is working for the
Japanese and all the guests were above suspicion, the
men were all released at 10.30 p.m.
Chang Shih-chow and his family who are
staying at the New Wei Chung Hotel (新味中旅舍) will

China Daily News and other local newspapers :-

STUDENTS OF A MIDDLE SCHOOL ON STRIKE

A serious dispute took place yesterday
at the Chiao Kwang Middle School (侨光中学), Ferry Road,
in the course of which 200 students surrounded their
Principal Wu Chien-chih (吴健之) and demanded his
resignation. This was flatly rejected and the Police
were notified. A number of officers were later detailed
to the school. A part of the students then withdrew from
the Principal's office taking with them a number of
documents, books, and other things and handed them for
safe custody to the School Support Committee.
Later an urgent meeting was convened by
the students, at which the following resolutions were
discussed and passed:-
(1) That the Board of Directors of the
school be asked to appoint a new Principal as soon as
possible.
(2) That a strike be declared from this
date.
(3) That the school authorities be
asked to return a part of the tuition fee to the students,
amounting to $10 each, within three days.
(4) That the students refuse to attend
school until the above demands have been complied with.
It is learned that the School Support
Committee has referred the matter to the Board of
Directors of the school.

1938年6月23日。晨间译件。

发自中央捕房。突击小队上楼。日本军官拔出手枪，命令房内所有人不得移动。客人们大为惊恐，因为他们中的一些人刚才正在讨论福州路同兴酒楼（Tung Shing Lou Restaurant）发生的谋杀案。警员礼貌地请所有女宾聚集在一个房间内等候检查。随后对所有男子进行了三次搜身，但未发现任何具有罪证性质的物品。
日本军官感到困惑不解。
经过一番讯问，他们得知主人是一位安分守己的亲日公民。但他们仍不放心，将主人、新郎及宾客带至中央捕房进行审讯。由于张世舟（Chang Shih-chow，音译）为日本人工作，且所有宾客均无可疑之处，这些男子于晚上10时30分全部获释。
目前居住在新味中旅舍（New Wei Chung Hotel）的张世舟及其家人，预计今日将返回周浦（Chowpu，音译）。

《中国日报》及其他本地报纸：

中学生罢工

昨日，位于斐伦路（Ferry Road）的侨光中学（Chiao Kwang Middle School）发生严重纠纷，期间200名学生围住校长吴健之（Wu Chien-chih），要求其辞职。这一要求被断然拒绝，警方随后接到通知。随后数名警员被派往该校。部分学生随后撤离校长办公室，带走了一些文件、书籍和其他物品，并将其移交校董会保管。
随后学生们召开紧急会议，讨论并通过了以下决议：
(1) 要求学校董事会尽快任命新校长。
(2) 自即日起宣布罢工。
(3) 要求校方在三天内向每位学生退还部分学费，金额为10元。
(4) 在上述要求得到满足之前，学生拒绝上课。
据悉，校董会已将此事转交学校董事会处理。

Translation of 10 letters seized at 31 Sing Mo An Li,
Taku Road.
------------------

(1) Dear Yue Zung,

Upon advice of my relatives, I had to stop home for the
new year. How is the situation in Shanghai. We are all alright.
Sugar and nuts received with thanks.

Ying Sung Foh
(No date)
------------------------------

(2) Dear Yue Zung,

Since the outbreak of the recent Sino-Japanese hostilities,
I removed my family to the country. Recently I have been told that
you had already returned to Shanghai, and I hope that you will be
able to find me a position in order to support myself and my family.
I am very sorry to tell you, that since the trouble started I have
been in a destitute condition.

Signed Zee Sing Yuen.
------------------------------

(3) Dear Yue Zung,

A letter addressed to you from Mr. Kwan has been received.
Please hand over the mlney to the bearer Mr. Van Chee Zung, who
will bring it back, or you may keep it for one or two days more,
as Mr. Kwan instructed to buy some goods with the money.

Yue,
April 4.
------------------------------

(4) Dear Yue Zung,

Arrived home on 2nd Jan. after 4 days spent on board the ship.
I paid $2.00 for registration, $13.00 for transportaion, $2.00 for food
stuffs, 50 cents for oil. I paid the $10.00 which I had borrowed from
you, please don't worry.

Tsai, 3rd, Jan.
------------------------------

(5) Dear Yue Zung,

On the 13th inst. I left Shanghai and arrived hame safely.

1937年12月1日。

---

(7) 丈夫岳宗：
收到10.00美元。给各位亲戚的礼物已按照你的指示 duly 分发。
日常工作中要小心，记得我们大家，不要在意别人的闲话。
年底需要购买很多东西，因此请尽快寄给我几美元。
通过张玲（Chang Ling）先生，我给你寄去一条床罩和一些腌制食品。我没能买到咸鱼，希望下次能买到一些。如果有空房，我可能会住在曹道松（Tseu Taoong Sung）（小萍的老师）家里。曹的地址是市场路（Rue du Marche）12号，就在市场对面。我不知道弄堂的名字。
你的妻子曹彩氏（Tsau Tsai Sz）
1938年1月9日。

---

(8) 丈夫岳宗：
我已收到你的来信。你是否收到了我通过张玲先生寄给你的床罩？
通过刘莲（Lau Lien）先生，我给你寄去半条咸鱼、一块咸肉和5只鸭子。

page_data.en:
- 3 -

On Lau Lien's return, please buy me 13 ft. of blue cotton
cloth (for children's long gowns), 2 pads of joss-paper (to
be used at the end of the year).

Send me some money before the Chinese new year, as it is
necessary at that time.

Your wife Tseu Tsai Sz.

P.S. Please ask Siau Ping has the Hong Ziang Shing Factory
started work yet.

Saung Ching.

------------------

(9) Mr. Zung Tsang,

The goods which you asked Ziang Ling to sell, were sold
to Zung Sing. Today Mr. Zung Yih called Ziang Ling to his home,
and on unwrapping the goods to examine same, it was found that
it contained no opium, but only a quantity of opium dregs, stones
and tea cakes. It was then alleged that Ziang Ling had defrauded
him of the money. It was not only wanted to get the money back,
but he also wanted to send Ziang Ling to the Police in order to
get him charged.

I should have brought the goods to Shanghai, but due to
the fact that I have no money to meet travelling expenses, I
am unable to do so.

I write this letter to inform you of the affair and wish
that you will go and interview Tsung Ding Yao Zung regarding the
occurrence.

Should Lee & Yao refuse to recognise the loss, please
inform me by next mail and I shall bring the goods to Shanghai
for negotiation, and all expenses incurred are to be paid by him.
Goods are to be kept at your place.

Best regards to Messrs Lee Tsung Ding, Yao Zung and Tseu
Yue Zung.

Signed Ying Vung Kwei,
11-4-/

------------------

(10) Dear Yue Zung,
page_data.zh:

刘莲回来时，请给我买13尺蓝棉布（用于做孩子的长衫），2刀冥纸（年底使用）。

春节前寄给我一些钱，因为那时急需。

你的妻子曹彩氏（Tseu Tsai Sz）。

附言：请问小萍， Hong Ziang Shing 工厂开工了吗？

Saung Ching。

你让江玲（Ziang Ling）出售的货物，已卖给宗兴（Zung Sing）。今天宗义（Zung Yih）先生把江玲叫到他家，拆开货物检查时发现，里面没有鸦片，只有一些鸦片渣、石头和茶饼。随后他声称江玲诈骗了他的钱财。他不仅想要回钱，还想把江玲送到警察局控告他。

我本应将货物带到上海，但由于我没有旅费，无法做到。

我写这封信是为了通知你这件事，并希望你能去拜访丁耀宗（Tsung Ding Yao Zung）先生，商谈此事。

如果李（Lee）和姚（Yao）拒绝承认损失，请在下一班邮件中通知我，我将把货物带到上海进行协商，所有产生的费用由他承担。货物暂存在你处。

向李宗丁（Lee Tsung Ding）、姚宗（Yao Zung）和徐岳宗（Tseu Yue Zung）诸位先生致意。

At 11a.m. on the 7/3/38 instructions were received

Inspector i/c of the Japanese Consular Police who had

forwarded by Mr. Tajima were handed to the undersigned.

1938年3月7日上午11时，收到日本籍助理警务处长（A.C.P.）小川（Kokegawa）先生的指示，要求就日本领事馆警察主管警官田岛（Tajima）督察所提供的情报进行调查。田岛督察从附属于日本总领事馆的 T. Kotah 警佐以及 A. Yamaguchi 和 T. Katsuko 警员处获得报告，称在四川路525号（由上海信托公司占用）为保护窗户而安装的装饰性铁栅栏上，注意到了日本天皇陛下（H.I.J.M.）的徽章标志。

日本领事当局希望工部局警务处提请该处所业主注意，此类徽章不应展示在上述建筑物上，因此根据日本当局的要求，请求通过必要的改动将其移除或遮盖。

四张由日本领事馆警察成员拍摄并由田岛先生转交的照片副本已交给下述签名人。

Telfer 侦探督察通知了“A”分区督察长，后者指示在采取任何行动之前先进行调查并提交报告。

Page 2.

D.S. Kobayashi visited the scene and ascertained
that the China Trust Co. is situated at 525 Szechuen Road
at the corner of Peking Road and there are 10 windows
to the offices, six of which face Peking Road and the
remainder Szechuan Road. Each of the windows has a
protective lattice style iron grill, the joints of which
are concealed by ornamental work in the shape of a
flower. In the case of two of the windows facing
Szechuen Road the flower designs on them are different to
the others but resemble the crest of the H.I.J.M. There
are 12 pieces of this design fixed at each window about
2½" in diameter and painted in gold colour.

As far as ascertained the China Trust Co. is a
Chinese concern.

This report is forwarded awaiting instructions.

第2页。

小林（Kobayashi）警佐前往现场勘查，查明中国信托公司（China Trust Co.）位于四川路525号，即北京路转角处。其办公室共有10扇窗户，其中6扇面向北京路，其余面向四川路。每扇窗户均装有保护性格栅式铁栏，其接合处由花形装饰件遮盖。在面向四川路的两扇窗户上，其花形图案与其他窗户不同，但类似于日本天皇陛下（H.I.J.M.）的徽章。每扇窗户上固定有12个此类图案饰件，直径约2½英寸，漆成金色。

经查，中国信托公司系一家华商机构。

本报告呈送，候示。
